request.deadline: 12 months from deployment; month-6 yield distribution; audit expected by July 1, 2026
deliverables: Deploy treasury-owned capital into Strike Finance V2 USDM liquidity infrastructure for 12 months
Return realized yield from the first six months to the Cardano Treasury at month 6
Return 100% of remaining treasury-owned deployed assets, including principal and realized yield minus any realized losses, at month 12
Provide monthly public transparency reports covering deployment, utilization, P&L, yield, drawdown, stablecoin exposure, market quality, distributions, and risks
Provide third-party assurance reports at deployment confirmation, month 6, and month 12
request.recipient: independent multisig council composed of Rami from Snek, Phil from Surf, and James from Monetra/Moneta as administrator
request.what: 12-month productive treasury deployment into Strike Finance V2 liquidity infrastructure, with ADA sold for USDM to provide stablecoin-denominated liquidity

claims.claim: The proposal requests 9,000,000 ADA for a 12-month liquidity deployment into Strike Finance V2 rather than grant funding.
The deployed ADA would be sold for USDM, modeled at ADA = 0.15 USD to create approximately 1,350,000 USDM of liquidity.
The deployment is modeled to generate approximately 135,000 USD or 900,000 ADA-equivalent in annual yield at a 10% USD-denominated APR, but returns are not guaranteed.

Strike claims it has processed over 1.13 billion USD in cumulative volume, facilitated about 968,000 to 1,001,000 trades, served over 3,000 unique traders, generated over 1.16 million USD in protocol revenue, and produced over 3.25 million USD in liquidity provider profit.
The document claims Strike represented over 50% of Cardano trading activity during the past six months.
Strike V2 data from March 20, 2026 through June 15, 2026 is presented as evidence of accelerating volume, revenue, trades, users, and open interest as liquidity increased.
The proposal states operational custody will be handled by an independent multisig council and that Strike Finance will not have unilateral custody or control of treasury assets.

The proposal identifies risks including ADA price appreciation risk, USDM depeg or redemption risk, smart contract risk, yield underperformance, liquidity risk, custody risk, and operational multisig risk.

Governance review is proposed if drawdown exceeds 8%, reporting is missed for two consecutive monthly cycles, or unresolved custody, accounting, stablecoin, redemption, or smart contract concerns arise, with mandatory review at 10% drawdown and wind-down review at 20% drawdown.

The proposal states Strike V2 has unofficial technical reviews and an official audit by Christian Schmitz expected to be finalized by July 1, 2026, but the completed audit is not included in the document.

summary: The document proposes deploying 9,000,000 ADA of treasury-owned capital into Strike Finance V2 liquidity for 12 months, converting it to USDM, targeting modeled yield and ecosystem liquidity growth, with independent multisig custody, reporting, assurance, and return-of-funds commitments, while acknowledging market, stablecoin, smart contract, custody, and underperformance risks.
